newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Travel to buy 51.7 pct of Sun Fook.
newsitem.headline: China Travel to buy 51.7 pct of Sun Fook.

text.p: China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd said on Monday it had agreed to buy 431.84 million shares, or a 51.66 percent stake, in Sun Fook Kong Holdings Ltd for HK$466.39 million, or HK$1.08 per share.

The company said in a statement it had also agreed to buy for HK$7.33 million in cash a total 31.88 million warrants, or 20.02 percent of Sun Fook's existing outstanding warrants, carrying the rights to subscribe for 31.88 million shares at HK$1.31 per share before June 30, 1999.
China Travel said it would make a cash offer for the remaining Sun Fook shares at HK$1.08 per share and for the remaining warrants at HK$0.23 per warrant.

The offer prices represented a discount of about 43.75 percent to the shares' last close of HK$1.92 and about 77.00 percent to the warrants' last traded price of HK$1.00 on May 14 before trading was suspended on May 15, the company said.

Sun Fook Kong also agreed to sell the entire issued share capital of three contruction companies, Sun Fook Kong Housing Services Ltd, Sun Fook Kong Construction Ltd and Intercede International Ltd Services Ltd to Shui Sing Holdings Corp for HK$64.29 million in cash, the statement said.
Shui Sing Holding Corp is controlled by Lo Ying Shek and his family, the existing controling shareholder of Sun Fook Kong.

China Travel said of the agreed purchase in Sun Fook Kong, Albert Chow, a former deputy managing director of Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, would acquire 66.87 million shares or eight percent of the company.
Its wholly-owned subsidiary, Winyear Profits Ltd, would acquire the remaining 364.97 million, representing about 43.66 percent of Sun Fook Kong, China Travel said.
Winyear Profits would also acquire all the 31.87 million warrants in Sun Fook Kong, it added.
Sun Fook Kong would appoint Chow as its managing director subject to shareholders' and the stock exchange's approvals, the statement said.
Upon Chow's appointment, Sun Fook Kong would issue 66.87 million new shares, or 7.41 percent of its enlarged issued share capital to Chow at HK$1.38 per share in cash.
The company would also issue to Chow a total of 120 million unlisted warrants to subscribe for the same number of new shares at HK$2.88 per share, it said.
Chow resigned certain major positions from Cheung Kong and its subsidiaries on April 30 and he is now a non-executive director of Cheung Kong.
Sun Fook Kong is an investment holding, construction and civil engineering company.
After the completion of the deals, the principal activities of the Sun Fook Kong group would be property development and investment and infrastructure investment, China Travel said.

Trading in shares and warrants of Sun Fook Kong will remain suspended until the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the stock exchange are satisfied that fair and orderly trading of the shares and warrants can take place, the statement said.
The SFC was conducting an enquiry into the trading activity of the shares and warrants of Sun Fook Kong in light of press reports regarding China Travel's future plans for the company, it added.
